jobs.name: ARCHITECTURE.md drift check
jobs.prompt:
A drift-detection script has run against ~/chubee/stack/ARCHITECTURE.md and its output is injected above as context.

If the script output is EMPTY or shows no drift: the architecture doc matches reality. Respond with EXACTLY the single word "SILENT" and nothing else — do not send any message to the user.

If the script output reports DRIFT (lines starting with "•"): the live system has diverged from what ARCHITECTURE.md documents. Do this:
1. Read ~/chubee/stack/ARCHITECTURE.md.
2. For each drift item, re-verify the live fact yourself (curl http://localhost:8000/v1/models, read ~/.hermes/config.yaml, docker ps, docker logs vllm-super for KV/concurrency numbers) — do not trust the script blindly, confirm with your own tool calls.
3. Update the affected section(s) of ARCHITECTURE.md to match reality (§2 measured tables, §3 running state, §5 build args, model tiers). Use the patch/write_file tools.
4. Bump the "Last verified" date at the top to today.
5. Then send the user a SHORT report: what drifted, what you changed in the doc, and whether anything looks like an unintended/accidental change they should know about (e.g. model silently reverted to OpenRouter, a container down, providers dict no longer empty).

Be surgical — only change what actually drifted. Preserve the doc's structure and the "why we chose Nemotron" reasoning. Never invent facts; every number in the doc must come from a live tool call you made this run.

jobs.name: arch-drift-check
jobs.prompt:
You are the architecture-doc drift watchdog for ChubeeAcer. A detector script has ALREADY RUN and its output is injected above as context.

DECISION RULE:
- If the injected script output is EMPTY / contains no "DRIFT DETECTED" line: the doc matches reality. Reply with exactly the single word SILENT and do nothing else. Send nothing to the user.
- If it contains a "DRIFT DETECTED" report: drift is real. Do the following:
  1. RE-VERIFY each flagged item yourself with your own tool calls (curl /v1/models, read ~/chubee/stack/.env, docker ps, curl localhost:6333/collections, read the doc). Do NOT trust the script blindly — it flags candidates; you confirm.
  2. For each CONFIRMED drift, surgically update ONLY the affected fact in ~/chubee/stack/ARCHITECTURE.md. PRESERVE all "why we chose X" reasoning prose — never rewrite the design-rationale sections. Never invent numbers; every figure must come from a live tool call you made this run.
  3. Append a dated bullet to the §10 Changelog describing what drifted and what you changed.
  4. Bump the "Last verified: YYYY-MM-DD" line at the top to today.
  5. Send the user a SHORT report: what drifted, what you changed, and flag anything that looks ACCIDENTAL or dangerous (e.g. the Hermes default model silently reverting from local Nemotron to a cloud provider, a container down, gpu-util mismatch). If something looks like an unintended regression, say so plainly and ask if they want it reverted.

Keep it terse. No preamble. The doc is the system-of-record; your job is to keep it true and surface surprises.

jobs.name: Daily email briefing
jobs.prompt:
Run the daily email triage for quintonschubee@gmail.com.

## Part 1: Inbox Triage

1. List all emails from the inbox:
   himalaya envelope list --page-size 50

2. For each unread email, categorize:
   - URGENT: security alerts, password resets, account lockouts, billing issues
   - IMPORTANT: bills, receipts, travel confirmations, shipping notifications, legal docs
   - PERSONAL: emails from known contacts, direct replies
   - NEWSLETTER: marketing, newsletters, promotions
   - JUNK: obvious spam, no-reply blasts

## Part 2: Hermes Update Check

3. Check for Hermes updates:
   cd ~/hermes-agent
   git fetch upstream --quiet
   BEHIND=$(git rev-list --count chubee-custom..upstream/main)
   echo "Commits behind upstream: $BEHIND"

4. If BEHIND > 0, get the critical commits:
   git log chubee-custom..upstream/main --oneline --no-merges | head -30
   Then scan these commit messages for: security, CVE, breaking, critical, permission, fix(docker), fix(gateway), fix(terminal). Highlight any that match these patterns.

5. Check desktop app version (the dashboard serves this):
   curl -s http://localhost:9119/api/status | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(f'Version: {d.get(\"version\",\"?\")}')" 2>/dev/null || echo "Dashboard not reachable"

## Part 3: Send Summary

6. Send a SINGLE email to qcalmus@gmail.com via himalaya:

   Subject: "Chubee Inbox Briefing — [date]"

   Body format:
   📬 Chubee Inbox Briefing — [date]
   ──────────────────────────────

   🔴 URGENT (N): [subject] — [sender]
   🟡 IMPORTANT (N): [subject] — [sender]
   🔵 PERSONAL (N): [subject] — [sender]
   ⚪ EVERYTHING ELSE (N): N newsletters/promos

   ──────────────────────────────
   🔧 HERMES STATUS
   Version: [version]
   Updates available: [N commits behind upstream]
   [If >0, list 3-5 most notable recent commits]
   [If any commit matches security/CVE/breaking, flag with ⚠️]

   Use `himalaya template send` piped via stdin.

7. If zero emails AND zero updates, send "Inbox zero, Hermes up to date — nothing to report."

Rules:
- ONE email per day. Never send multiple.
- Never reply to individual emails without explicit permission.
- Default to lower-urgency if ambiguous.
- One line per item: sender + subject.
- Do NOT mark emails as read.
